newsitem.title: UK: US oil refinery maintenance heavy this spring - IEA.
newsitem.headline: US oil refinery maintenance heavy this spring - IEA.

text.p: Oil refinery shutdowns for maintenance this spring are expected to be heavier than normal in the United States but little changed from previous years in Europe and Asia, said the International Energy Agency (IEA) on Friday.

The peak in U.S. shutdowns is expected to occur in February with a larger-than-usual volume of refining capacity out of operation in the coming three months, the IEA said in latest Monthly Oil Market Report.

But there is some flexibility on the timing of turnarounds and the extent of maintenance shutdowns may well be influenced by the U.S. gas oil and gasoline inventory situation and by weather conditions. A larger than normal volume of cracking capacity (of the gasoline type) is scheduled to be out of operation in the U.S. during the next three months.
Refinery shutdowns in Europe and Asia are expected to follow normal patterns during this spring with the peak occurring later than in the U.S.
Early European spring maintenance will be mainly concentrated in the Mediterranean.
